body.p: Roles in apply at different scopes. Some roles define administrative privileges, others define product functionality, and others control access to specific resources or workflows.

section.title: Organization level roles
section.p: In Cloud all the content is managed within an organization workspace. Users are invited to join an organization and are assigned an organization-level role that determines their administrative privileges within that organization.

There are two organization-level roles:
Member is the default organization-level role.
Users with the Member role can:
Access the organization workspace
Perform actions permitted by their assigned user role
Admin is the Organization Administrator organization-level role that provides administrative privileges for the entire organization. The user who creates the organization receives this role.
Users with this role can:
Edit organization settings
Manage organization users (invite, remove, or update users)
Assign organization-level roles
Manage license allocation within the organization

section.title: User Roles
section.p:
User roles define what functionality a user can access in . There are two user roles available:
Subject-Matter Expert is the default user role.
Users with this role have access only to review functionality. They can:
Access review tasks assigned to them
Read the documents included in review tasks
Add comments and suggestions
Can create and manage independent (not project releated) review tasks
Author is the advanced user role.
Users with this role have access to the full functionality, in addition to what SMEs can do, they can:
Access and manage projects
Create and manage project review tasks
Integrate review feedback
Manage and publish deliverables
Access to AI functionality
A user role is associated with a license type, provides licenses packages that specify the available licenses for Subject Matter Experts and for Authors.

section.title: Project Roles
section.p: Within a project, there is an implicit role associated with the user who creates the project, the project owner while the other users that have access to the project are project members. Project access is determined by project visibility (public or private) and project ownership.

li.p: Member is the role of users who have access to a project.
Project membership is determined depending on the project visibility:
All users with the Author user role automatically become members of the project.

Only users explicitly invited by the project owner can access the project. In private projects, the project owner controls the list of project members and determines who can access and work within the project.
Owner is the user who creates the project. This user has additional administrative privileges related to managing the project.
For example, the project owner can:
Configure project settings.
Add or remove project members (for private projects).
Delete the project.

section.title: Review Task Roles
section.p: Within a review task, users can have different roles that determine how they participate in the review process.

li.p: Reviewer is the default role assigned to users participating in a review task.
Users with this role are responsible for providing feedback on the content under review.
Reviewers can:
Access the review task content
Read the documents included in the review
Add comments and suggestions
Reply to other comments
Participate in discussions related to the review
This role is typically assigned to Subject-Matter Experts (SMEs) or other contributors who are asked to review the task content.
Owner is the role assigned to the user who created the review task or to users that were granted this role by another task owner.
Users with this role can:
Edit review task settings
Manage access to the review task
Assign review task roles to other users
Control the workflow state of the review task
Integrate the accepted changes from the review task into the original content repository
